result:
The code queues an issue-created webhook, but **it does not actually call the customer’s endpoint**. The delivery job simulates delivery by computing a signature, logging the attempt, and marking the row delivered. It also computes a backoff value but does not schedule retries.

The path starts in [the new-issue page](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/168a02b4-6dbd-4b17-a572-be6a3190e2e6/src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/issues/new/page.tsx), which passes `createIssueAction` to `IssueForm`. In [issue-form.tsx](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/168a02b4-6dbd-4b17-a572-be6a3190e2e6/src/components/domain/issue/issue-form.tsx), the form validates with `createIssueSchema` and submits through that action. [create-issue.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/168a02b4-6dbd-4b17-a572-be6a3190e2e6/src/actions/issues/create-issue.ts) uses `withAction` to validate again and resolve the actor, checks permission and the project’s quota, and calls `createIssue`.

In [issue-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/168a02b4-6dbd-4b17-a572-be6a3190e2e6/src/server/services/issue-service.ts), `createIssue` checks organization scope, the project, permission and quota, allocates an issue number, and inserts the issue. It then awaits `emit("issue.created", ...)`, carrying the actor envelope plus the issue ID, project ID, title, assignee and priority. The in-process `emit` in [event-bus.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/168a02b4-6dbd-4b17-a572-be6a3190e2e6/src/lib/event-bus.ts) waits for subscribers to settle, but isolates their errors rather than failing issue creation.

The webhook subscriber is installed at server startup: `registerEventHandlers` in [event-registry.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/168a02b4-6dbd-4b17-a572-be6a3190e2e6/src/server/services/event-registry.ts) calls `registerWebhookListeners` in [webhook-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/168a02b4-6dbd-4b17-a572-be6a3190e2e6/src/server/services/webhook-service.ts). Its `issue.created` listener serializes the event and calls `enqueueForOrg`. That function uses `listEndpoints` in [webhook-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/168a02b4-6dbd-4b17-a572-be6a3190e2e6/src/server/repositories/webhook-repository.ts) to find endpoints belonging to the event’s organization, skips disabled endpoints and those whose stored event-type list does not include `issue.created`, and calls `enqueueDelivery` for each match. Each delivery begins as a pending database row with zero attempts.

A later authenticated cron `POST` to [webhook-delivery/route.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/168a02b4-6dbd-4b17-a572-be6a3190e2e6/src/app/api/cron/webhook-delivery/route.ts) calls `runWebhookDeliveryJob` in [webhook-delivery-job.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/168a02b4-6dbd-4b17-a572-be6a3190e2e6/src/server/jobs/webhook-delivery-job.ts). It claims up to 25 pending rows; `claimPendingDeliveries` increments each attempt count. The job checks the organization’s plan and feature flag, the attempt limit, and whether the endpoint still exists and is enabled. Those failed checks mark the row failed. Otherwise it signs the stored payload, logs the endpoint and an abbreviated signature, and calls `markDelivered`—there is no outbound HTTP request.

`backoffMs` calculates exponential delays of one second, two seconds, four seconds and so on, capped at five minutes, and the job gives up when a claimed row has more than six attempts. However, the calculated delay is only logged: there is no send failure to detect or retry scheduling in this implementation. A row left pending, for example after a worker crash, can be claimed on a later run, but the code does not enforce the calculated delay.

For authentication, `createWebhook` generates a per-endpoint secret when the endpoint is registered. `signPayload` computes a hex-encoded HMAC-SHA256 over the exact UTF-8 payload string using that secret. A receiver would recompute the HMAC over the exact raw body and compare it with the supplied signature. The current delivery job sends neither body nor signature; the [test route](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/168a02b4-6dbd-4b17-a572-be6a3190e2e6/src/app/api/webhooks/[endpointId]/test/route.ts) returns a sample payload and full signature so a customer can check their verification logic.
